Research question: Which seed-mix species establish, persist and self-seed in each Ontario ELC  ecosite type (e.g. dry/wet deciduous forest, meadow, riparian)?

Retrieved evidence from 1 unique publications (1 graph edges).

PUBLICATION FINDINGS

1. Long-term functionality of woody debris structures for forest-floor small mammals on clearcuts
Sullivan, Thomas P., Sullivan, Druscilla S. | 2019 | Forest Ecology and Management | 10.1016/j.foreco.2019.117535
Retrieved findings:
- treatment site type (dispersed sites) -> higher mean winter survival of M. gapperi: mean winter survival was significantly (F3,6 = 6.46; P = 0.04) different, among treatment sites with declining survival from the dispersed to forest sites

OVERALL INTERPRETATION
The retrieved relationships describe the findings reported in these publications. They should not be interpreted as a direct answer to every part of the research question. Assess the relevance of each publication before drawing a conclusion.
These results represent retrieved graph evidence, not a comprehensive review of all scientific literature. Different outcomes, species, sites and treatments should not be treated as directly comparable.

Research question: For tree planting in Canadian forest restoration, how do planting-stock traits (seedling size, nursery fertilization, mycorrhizal inoculation) affect survival and growth, and how do competing vegetation and site preparation change that? Retrieved evidence from 4 unique publications (20 graph edges). PUBLICATION FINDINGS 1. Silviculture and planted species interact to influence reforestation success on a Kalmia -dominated site – a 15-year study Thiffaul, Nelson, Titus, Brian D, Moroni, Martin T | 2010 | The Forestry Chronicle | 10.5558/tfc86234-2 Retrieved findings: - fertilization at planting -> Increased growth of black spruce: The use of herbicide significantly increased 15-year GLD and volume index of all three conifer species, but only black spruce responded positively to fertilization at planting. - fertilization at planting -> Growth of jack pine: The use of herbicide significantly increased 15-year GLD and volume index of all three conifer species, but only black spruce responded positively to fertilization at planting. 2. Exponential fertilization promotes seedling growth by increasing nitrogen retranslocation in trembling aspen planted for oil sands reclamation Pokharel, P., Chang, S.X. | 2016 | Forest Ecology and Management | 10.1016/j.foreco.2016.03.034 Retrieved findings: - Exponential fertilization -> Increased seedling biomass: Exponential fertilization increased new stem, old stem, root, and total biomass in the first growing season and leaf, new stem and total biomass in the second growing season (all P < 0.05) on the PMM site. - Exponential fertilization -> Increased seedling biomass: On the LFH site, the increase (by 34%) was in new stem biomass (P = 0.03) during the first growing season and leaf (by 50%, P = 0.02), new stem (by 69%, P = 0.01), old stem (by 41%, P < 0.01) and total biomass (by 36%, P < 0.01) in the second growing season. 3. Nitrogen recovery in planted seedlings, competing vegetation, and soil in response to fertilization on a boreal mine reclamation site Sloan, Joshua L., Uscola, Mercedes, Jacobs, Douglass F. | 2016 | Forest Ecology and Management | 10.1016/j.foreco.2015.10.024 Retrieved findings: - controlled-release fertilizer application -> increased diameter growth of seedlings: seedlings that had received CRF out-performing unfertilized seedlings - controlled-release fertilizer application -> increased organ biomass of seedlings: Average organ biomass of seedlings that had received CRF increased significantly compared with those that received either no fertilizer or IAF. 4. How to shift unproductive Kalmia angustifolia – Rhododendron groenlandicum heath to productive conifer plantation Thiffault, Nelson, Jobidon, Robert | 2006 | Canadian Journal of Forest Research | 10.1139/x06-090 Retrieved findings: - fertilization with Forest Paks -> increased aboveground biomass: Independently of scarification or initial N concentration, seedlings fertilized with Forest Paks (F1) had greater aboveground biomass than seedlings fertilized with Silva Paks (F2) (Table 3). - fertilization with Forest Paks -> increased effect of scarification on aboveground biomass: The positive effect of scarification (either S1 or S2) on GLD and biomass was enhanced when seedlings were fertilized (with either F1 or F2) (Table 3, Fig. 3). OVERALL INTERPRETATION The retrieved relationships describe the findings reported in these publications. They should not be interpreted as a direct answer to every part of the research question. Assess the relevance of each publication before drawing a conclusion. These results represent retrieved graph evidence, not a comprehensive review of all scientific literature. Different outcomes, species, sites and treatments should not be treated as directly comparable.
